item.title: Denmark's EIFO joins TEKEVER's $580M Series D as company expands into Odense
item.description: Defencetech TEKEVER today announced plans to establish an operational presence in Odense, Denmark, its first in the Nordic region, to support its work across the region. The announcement follows a mee...
item.content:encoded:
Defencetech TEKEVER today announced plans to establish an operational presence in Odense, Denmark, its first in the Nordic region, to support its work across the region. The announcement follows a meeting in Copenhagen with Denmark’s Minister of Defence, Jeppe Bruus.

TEKEVER develops and provides AI-centric autonomous systems for defence, security and civil applications.

 Alongside plans to establish an operational presence in Denmark, TEKEVER will welcome EIFO, the Export and Investment Fund of Denmark, as an investor.  EIFO has committed to joining the closing of TEKEVER’s $580 million Series D financing round, first announced on 23 September 2026 at a valuation of $6.4 billion.


TEKEVER is progressing the creation of a Danish entity and the arrangements for its local operations. It will develop its operational presence in phases, in response to demand and approvals.

item.title: MucoLife Therapeutics secures €91K from Vinnova to scale manufacturing of COPD treatment
item.description: MucoLife Therapeutics has received €91,000 (SEK 1 million) from Vinnova, Sweden’s innovation agency, through the call “Support to small and medium-sized companies for the use of life science infrastru...
item.content:encoded:
MucoLife Therapeutics has received €91,000 (SEK 1 million) from Vinnova, Sweden’s innovation agency, through the call “Support to small and medium-sized companies for the use of life science infrastructure.”

The funding supports establishing a scalable manufacturing process for MLT-001, the company’s first-in-class inhaled peptide designed to dissolve airway mucus plugs in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).

Check out our earlier interview with Thaher Pelaseyed, co-founder and CEO at MucoLife Therapeutics

Mucus plugging is present in more than half of patients with moderate-to-severe COPD, and no approved therapy targets it directly.

Mucus obstruction is a relevant disease feature associated with poor outcomes, including reduced lung function, more exacerbations and increased mortality, and it can be targeted for the benefit of patients.

MucoLife’s work has shown that the synthesis of MLT-001 is scalable, and the grant will be used to develop the process of scaled-up manufacturing.

item.title: Fourthline and Veridas combine forces to take on global digital identity market
item.description: Digital ID provider Veridas is merging with European identity verification and compliance company Fourthline to deliver an advanced trust platform across Europe and the Americas. European investment A...
item.content:encoded:
Digital ID provider Veridas is merging with European identity verification and compliance company Fourthline to deliver an advanced trust platform across Europe and the Americas. European investment Ashgrove has committed a €40 million growth investment to Fourthline to support the completion of its merger with Veridas. The wider funding package of up to €65 million includes support from Fourthline’s existing shareholder Finch Capital and new equity investment from Seaya Andromeda.

Founded in Amsterdam in 2017, Fourthline enables financial institutions to maintain consistent compliance standards while supporting ambitious global expansion. Its clients include  Revolut, N26, Trade Republic, Qonto, Scalable Capital, Scalapay, Raisin, Rabobank and Bitpanda.

item.title: From fallen leaves to factory floors: How Releaf is making alternative paper commercially viable
item.description: Ukrainian-founded, Paris-based Releaf is developing an alternative to conventional wood-based paper by transforming urban fallen leaves into fibres for packaging, paper and other materials. The compan...
item.content:encoded:
Ukrainian-founded, Paris-based Releaf is developing an alternative to conventional wood-based paper by transforming urban fallen leaves into fibres for packaging, paper and other materials. The company is not only a boost for the circular economy but has enabled established paper producers to integrate its materials into existing industrial processes rather than building an entirely new manufacturing ecosystem.

I spoke to Valentyn Frechka, founder and CEO of Releaf, to learn more.

From scientific breakthrough to commercial reality

While many startups have demonstrated that alternative materials work scientifically, commercialisation remains a major obstacle. According to Frechka, success depends on two factors: positioning and proximity to both raw materials and customers.

“If you position yourself as a breakthrough company that's going to compete directly with major corporations, you're already putting yourself in a difficult position.

item.title: OpenAI “catalyst” for startups, says European executive, amid startup application layer concerns
item.description: OpenAI is a “catalyst” for European startups, according to one of its top European executives, despite admitting there is “tension” between the ChatGPT developer and its European startup clients over ...
item.content:encoded:
OpenAI is a “catalyst” for European startups, according to one of its top European executives, despite admitting there is “tension” between the ChatGPT developer and its European startup clients over OpenAI launching rival products. Tricia Troth, head of go-to-market, startups EMEA, OpenAI, responded to a question about OpenAI potentially shifting more from selling AI model access to owning the applications built around the technology.

Troth said: “We are here to be the catalyst for most of these startups. That is what we want to do. We actually work very closely with a lot of startups where we see that kind of tension, bringing them into the fold."

Troth pointed to Swedish legaltech Legora as an example in which OpenAI works with a startup it arguably competes with, after OpenAI launched a dedicated legal offering Astra for Law earlier this year.

Troth said OpenAI and Legora co-developed a legal plug in together.

item.title: Vensum Power raises €9M to cut power losses in AI data centres, EV charging and energy storage
item.description: Finnish deeptech companyVensum Power has raised €9 million in a Series A funding round co-led byLifeline Ventures, Larsen & Toubro Group and Eviny Ventures. The investmentwill support the mass pro...
item.content:encoded:
Finnish deeptech company Vensum Power has raised €9 million in a Series A funding round co-led by Lifeline Ventures, Larsen & Toubro Group and Eviny Ventures. The investment will support the mass production of its power conversion technology and its expansion into AI data centres. The new funding brings Vensum Power's total capital raised to €15.2 million.

Vensum Power develops a software-defined power conversion platform designed to improve energy efficiency by reducing electricity losses during power conversion. Its technology is intended for applications including electric vehicle (EV) charging, energy storage systems and DC microgrids.

item.title: UK Sovereign AI fund and Stripe CEO back Potential Sciences in multi-million-dollar raise
item.description: A London-based startup building AI infrastructure for scientific drug discovery has received backing from the UK government’s Sovereign AI fund and Stripe CEO Patrick Collison.Potential Sciences lever...
item.content:encoded:
A London-based startup building AI infrastructure for scientific drug discovery has received backing from the UK government’s Sovereign AI fund and Stripe CEO Patrick Collison.

Potential Sciences leverages AI, machine learning and quantum chemistry simulations to help researchers understand how molecules behave and interact. It is pioneering a new approach, with an AI model focused on the fundamental laws of physics, rather than previous experimental data, the startup says. It says this could make the AI calculations needed to design chemicals 100 times cheaper than at present.

The government’s Sovereign AI fund today confirmed it was backing Potential Sciences, as part of a raise in the tens of millions of dollars. The Sovereign AI fund is also committing compute capacity to Potential Sciences, which was founded in November last year.

It marks the latest bet by the UK government's Sovereign AI fund, whose mission is to ensure that the UK develops, owns and scales key AI firms. Its other bets include chip startup Olix and AI startups Ineffable Intelligence and Callosum.

item.title: Five UK startups secure eight patents from Panasonic, Nokia, NEC and DENSO
item.description: Five UK startups have won the rights to patented technologies developed by some of the world's largest corporations, a prize that could transform their ability to compete at home and internationally. ...
item.content:encoded:
Five UK startups have won the rights to patented technologies developed by some of the world's largest corporations, a prize that could transform their ability to compete at home and internationally. 

The five winners of IPHatch UK 2026 have secured eight patents originating from Panasonic,  Nokia, NEC and DENSO, giving them access to innovations that would ordinarily be far beyond the reach of young businesses.  The achievement follows a highly competitive selection process for the fourth annual UK  competition.

Twenty-one startups were shortlisted for the final pitch day at City of Glasgow  College, and five were selected.  Winners also gain a direct relationship with the corporations behind the technology, which could open doors to future collaboration, investment and international markets.  The five successful companies are: 

• CALMS International (West Midlands), an enterprise software company, awarded  an NEC patent 

• Cyber Nandhini (Aberdeen), a cybersecurity business, awarded a Nokia patent

• The Discourse AI

item.title: Claimlane bags €5.6M to turn product claims into business value
item.description: Aftersales product resolution platform Claimlane has raised €5.6million in a Series A funding round led by Verb Ventures, with participationfrom Skagerak Capital and Vendep Capital. The investment wil...
item.content:encoded:
Aftersales product resolution platform Claimlane has raised €5.6 million in a Series A funding round led by Verb Ventures, with participation from Skagerak Capital and Vendep Capital. The investment will support the development of customer-specific AI agents and the company's expansion in the United States.

Claimlane develops a platform that helps brands and retailers manage product-related issues, including warranty claims, repairs, replacements, refunds and supplier coordination. Its customers include Skechers, Black Diamond, tonies and Hummel.

Handling faulty or damaged products often involves multiple parties across the supply chain, from retailers and manufacturers to suppliers and repair partners. These processes can be complex and time-consuming, particularly when businesses rely on disconnected systems to assess claims, determine responsibility and coordinate resolutions.
